title: Cheat's Sushi
subtitle: with Omelette and Avo
description: Get the whole family involved with this delicious cheat's sushi using kid-friendly omelette instead of seaweed. Lay out the soft rice, avo and wasabi, then let everyone roll up themselves.

steps.text: Cook rice: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear. Put in a small saucepan with 250ml (1 cup) water, cover and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce the heat to low and cook for 12 mins or until tender and the water is absorbed. Turn off the heat and stand, covered, for at least 5 mins.

Prep ingredients: Meanwhile, peel the carrot, then shred with a julienne peeler or coarsely grate with a box grater. Thinly slice the capsicum and avocado. Whisk 2 eggs, 2 tsp soy sauce and 2 tsp water in a bowl until well combined.

Cook omelettes: Heat 2 tsp vegetable oil in a medium frypan over medium heat. Add half the egg mixture, swirl to coat the base of the pan and cook for 1-2 mins on one side until set. Remove from pan and repeat with another 2 tsp vegetable oil and the remaining egg mixture to make 2 thin omelettes. Remove from the pan.

Cook veggies: Heat 2 tsp vegetable oil in the pan over medium heat. Cook the carrot and capsicum, stirring, for 3-4 mins until softened. Stir in 1 tbs mirin and 1 tbs soy sauce and cook for a further 1-2 mins until warmed through. Remove from the heat.

Roll up and serve: Add 1 tbs mirin and 1 tbs white vinegar to the cooked rice and stir well. Divide the omelettes among plates and spread with the wasabi (see Kitchen tips). Lay the rice in a line on the omelette, just off centre, and top with the vegetables and avocado. Roll up into sushi rolls (see Kitchen tips) and cut into 5cm pieces. Serve with soy sauce to dip, if desired.

Kitchen tips: If you prefer less heat or are serving this to little ones, add the wasabi to taste or leave it out and serve at the table (mix it into the soy sauce, for dipping). To help roll the sushi, use a piece of baking paper or a sushi mat if you have one.
